c1-13.title: Drugs and addiction
c1-13.story: For her pharmacology seminar, Anna interviewed her grandfather, a retired hospital doctor. He explained that [[opium]], made from a kind of poppy, was once sold freely in pharmacies across Europe. Doctors later refined it into [[morphine]], which he still considers one of the most valuable painkillers in medicine. The trouble, he said, is that every [[opiate]] carries a serious risk of dependence, even when it is prescribed. In his clinic, patients trying to quit heroin received [[methadone]] under strict supervision. He also described young people brought in after taking [[amphetamine]] at parties, often with dangerously racing hearts. Some had used [[meth]], which he called the most destructive substance he had ever seen. When Anna asked about [[cannabis]] and [[LSD]], he admitted that the science is more complicated than most headlines suggest. By the end, Anna had three pages of notes and a new respect for her grandfather's patience. Her professor later gave the interview the highest mark in the class.

c1-14.title: In the emergency room
c1-14.story: When Anna's dad woke up with a sharp pain in his [[abdomen]], Mama drove him straight to the emergency room. At [[triage]], a nurse checked his pulse and moved him ahead of several other patients. The doctor was worried about his [[aorta]], so she ordered an urgent scan. Luckily, the problem turned out to be a muscle [[spasm]], painful but harmless. For a small procedure, he received a local [[anesthetic]] rather than general [[anesthesia]]. Afterward, a nurse placed a [[catheter]] in his arm to give him fluids. When he stood up too quickly, a wave of [[vertigo]] sent him straight back to bed. Anna, waiting nervously in the hallway, noticed that the old [[tic]] in her eye had returned. By evening he was home, joking that the hospital coffee had been the worst part.

c1-15.title: Diseases and germs
c1-15.story: Anna and Ira spent Sunday preparing for their microbiology exam at the kitchen table. Ira quizzed her on how a [[pathogen]] differs from a [[toxin]], which can harm the body without any living germ. They reviewed [[cholera]], which still spreads wherever clean water is scarce, and [[Ebola]], whose outbreaks require strict isolation. Anna then drew the entire digestive [[tract]], from the mouth to the [[anus]], and labeled each organ. After that, they moved on to blood disorders. Ira explained that [[anemia]] often just means too little iron, while [[leukemia]] is a cancer of the blood cells. Taras wandered in, glanced at the diagram, and announced that he had lost his appetite. The girls laughed, and a week later both of them passed the exam.

c1-16.title: Hormones and the brain
c1-16.story: Lisa had to give a presentation on hormones, and she felt a rush of [[adrenaline]] before she said a word. She began with the [[neuron]], explaining how these cells pass signals throughout the brain. Next she described [[serotonin]], a chemical that helps regulate mood and sleep. She mentioned that an [[antidepressant]] often works by changing how the brain uses it. Then she compared [[testosterone]] and [[estrogen]], noting that both are present in every body, just in different amounts. Finally, she talked about her grandfather, who injects [[insulin]] before every meal because of his diabetes. By the end, her voice was steady and the class applauded. Afterward, Anna joked that Lisa had demonstrated the first hormone on her list perfectly.

c1-17.title: The mind and memory
c1-17.story: Max's psychology course had reached the unit on the mind, and he kept telling Anna about it over coffee. In one study, half the volunteers received a sugar pill as a [[placebo]], yet many of them reported feeling better. The professor called this the [[placebo effect]] and warned that it makes testing new medicines difficult. They also discussed [[amnesia]], and Max admitted he had assumed it only happened in films. A guest speaker with [[autism]] described how she experiences noise and crowds, which Max found eye-opening. Another lecture covered [[mania]], when a person may barely sleep and feel unstoppable for days. Anna teased him that his [[ego]] had grown since he started the course. Max laughed and said his [[alter ego]], "Doctor Max," was simply sharing his wisdom. Then he forgot where he had parked his bike, and Anna diagnosed him with very selective memory.

c1-18.title: A family wedding
c1-18.story: Max's sister Sofia got married in June, and their entire [[clan]] gathered at the grandparents' country house. Sofia wore a delicate silver [[tiara]] that had belonged to her great-grandmother. Her [[bouquet]] was made of white blossoms from the old [[magnolia]] by the gate. Grandma had lined the garden path with pink [[azaleas|azalea]] and deep red [[dahlias|dahlia]]. Max's grandfather spent most of the evening with an old army [[comrade]] he had not seen in forty years. Meanwhile, Anna and Max arranged a secret [[rendezvous]] by the cake table, hoping to grab the first slices. When they got there, Anna's little brother Taras was already waiting, with frosting on his chin.

c1-19.title: Family characters
c1-19.story: At every family dinner, Anna enjoys noticing how different everyone's personality is. Her mama has a calm [[temperament]] and rarely raises her voice, even when the oven breaks. Her dad, a born [[realist]], always brings an umbrella and a backup plan. Max, who is invited every year, plays the [[buffoon]] and tells silly jokes until Taras nearly falls off his chair. Grandpa was apparently a [[dandy]] in his youth, famous for his silk ties and polished shoes. Grandma insists he was never a [[playboy]], though she admits half the town admired him. This year, he still bowed to Anna at the door and said, "Good evening, [[mademoiselle]]." Anna rolled her eyes, but secretly she loved it.

c1-20.title: Job interview
c1-20.story: After finishing her [[doctorate]] in chemistry, Max's sister Sofia started looking for her first industry job. A former classmate she had met through [[networking]] passed her name to a [[recruiter]] at a medical lab. At the interview, she presented a [[portfolio]] of her research projects, neatly organized by topic. The panel was impressed by her [[professionalism]] when the projector failed and she calmly continued from printed slides. One interviewer turned out to share her [[alma mater]], and they briefly compared memories of the same strict professor. When asked about her weaknesses, she answered with [[tact]], admitting that she sometimes takes on too much. Then she asked about [[work-life balance]], since she wanted her evenings free for her new husband. A week later, the lab called with an offer, and the whole family celebrated with cake.
